reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a PancakeSwap/Binance Smart Chain front-running bot through a linked contract that viewers are instructed to deploy and fund with BNB. It claims easy passive income, prior multi-BNB returns, and a rapid 0.24 BNB return from a 0.5 BNB investment, while stating that adding more BNB can increase possible profit. Risk disclaimers are present but accompany these direct funding instructions and profit claims.

citations.quote: PancakeSwap Front Running Bot 2022 - EASY TUTORIAL (NO DOWNLOAD)
We are going to be coding our very own front-runner bot contract to run on PancakeSwap on the Binance Smart Chain.
we need to go to our internet browser and head over to remix.theorem.org.
it is going to allow us to inject our transaction with a higher gas fee one good way higher than the transaction that is trying to be entered, this will allow our transaction to be processed first
the victim transaction gets sandwiched between ours and we make a small profit off the slippage difference in the transaction

opening.argument: The presentation does not promise a certain investment result. Its accompanying notice expressly says cryptocurrency is highly volatile and high-risk, that the speaker does not guarantee any particular outcome, and that viewers should do their own research before investing. The speaker also warns that the bot can buy into contracts that are not profitable and tells viewers it is at their own risk. Those warnings materially qualify the discussion of possible returns: this is conditional, speculative content, not a representation that funding the contract will reliably produce income.

citations.quote: Cryptocurrency is HIGHLY volatile and a very high-risk investment.
The speaker does not guarantee any particular outcome.
sometimes it can buy into contracts that aren't profitable
however it is at your at your own risk

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited funding instructions show how the demonstration operates, but they do not establish a deceptive guarantee. The same material expressly warns of volatility, possible losses, and no guaranteed outcome. A tutorial may explain a risky mechanism while disclosing that the result is uncertain; the presence of instructions alone does not prove that the speaker concealed those risks.

citations.quote: The speaker does not guarantee any particular outcome.
Trading cryptocurrencies poses considerable risk of loss.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings do not neutralize the central solicitation. The video still presents funding the contract as the next step and says greater funding can produce greater profit. More importantly, it describes the activity as “very easy passive income” and reports a rapid return, while the disclaimer merely shifts risk to viewers. Saying outcomes are not guaranteed does not make those persuasive profit claims reliable.

the more you put in the larger the transaction you'll be able to front run, and the more profit you'll be able to make
0.24 bnb is already full what was that like two maybe three minutes off a 0.5 bnb investment

opening.argument: The content is presented as an operational programming tutorial. The title calls it an “EASY TUTORIAL,” and the speaker walks through creating a Solidity file, compiling it in Remix, and connecting a wallet. The supplied frames likewise show a code editor, compiler interface, transaction controls, and wallet interface. That is consistent with teaching or demonstrating blockchain tooling and contract operation. Explaining how a system is purported to work, including a risky trading strategy, does not by itself certify the strategy or promise viewers a return.

citations.quote: PancakeSwap Front Running Bot 2022 - EASY TUTORIAL (NO DOWNLOAD)
The remis is an application that was developed to allow us to develop, compile, launch and transact with smart contracts
we are going to compile our contract in Remix

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not make the content a solicitation. The cited passages describe coding and deployment steps, but they do not establish that the speaker is selling access, collecting deposits, or guaranteeing success. The material also identifies uncertainty and possible honeypots, which is compatible with a demonstration of a claimed tool rather than certification that it is safe or profitable.

citations.quote: Unless it's open source. And I hope you guys wouldn't either.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This is more than abstract education: viewers are told to deploy the contract, fund it with BNB, and press the action control. The speaker then claims a 0.24 BNB return from 0.5 BNB in minutes and describes the process as profitable. A tutorial format does not change the practical effect of directing viewers through a funding workflow while promoting claimed returns.

opening.argument: The evidence does not establish several features ordinarily associated with a deposit-return scam. It does not show a request for passwords or credentials, a downline or referral structure, or a guaranteed return. Instead, the description characterizes the material as educational, says the speaker is not a licensed adviser, and warns viewers never to invest more than they can afford to lose. The video discusses software and a speculative transaction process; the existence of a BNB funding step does not, without proof of deceptive control over the funds or guaranteed repayment, establish a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: This content is NOT to be considered as financial advice, legal advice or taxation advice of any kind.
The speaker does not guarantee any particular outcome.
never invest more than you can afford to lose
it could be a honeypot or some kind of coin contract who knows

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies a funding instruction and profit language, but that is not proof that the creator controlled viewers' funds or fabricated a result. The record does not show credential collection, a recruitment scheme, or a guaranteed repayment promise. The described process may be a risky software demonstration whose commercial or technical claims require independent verification, rather than an established scam.

citations.quote: The speaker does not guarantee any particular outcome.
it is at your at your own risk

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam classification does not require every possible mechanism. Here, the creator directs viewers to deploy and fund a contract, says more BNB means more profit, and presents a quick return as evidence. The absence of a password request or downline is therefore beside the point. The disclaimer confirms risk but does not rebut the concrete inducement to place BNB into the promoted workflow.
